messages:
cora: Heads-up — noticed a 15-25% perf regression on heavy-batched paged-KV workloads after yesterday's epilogue prefetch tweak. Profiling attached. Suspect the hotspot sampler is biasing the kernel chooser toward packed-QKV + eager-epilogue which thrashes L2. Anyone else seeing this?

jin: Repro'd on my workstation. With B=64, S=1024 the chooser picks Packed+Eager. CPU / GPU timelines show repeated eviction spikes. Quick perf summary: 
```
# fused_attn_bench --batch 64 --seq 1024 --kv paged
old: 1.00x baseline
new: 0.78x (regression ~22%)
L2 miss rate +34% on kernel hot path
```

alex_m: Can you paste the full perf flame or the kernel selector log? I want to see the chooser scoring.

cora: Pasting excerpt from selector log: 
```
[selector] candidates: packed_qkv_soft_epilogue (score 0.84)
[selector] candidates: separate_qkv_lazy_epilogue (score 0.47)
[heuristic] batch_penalty=0.12 seq_penalty=0.05 kv_hotness_bonus=0.40
```

matteo: kv_hotness_bonus is coming from the hotspot sampler which looks at recent KV hit density per key. If the sampler overweights short-term spikes, it can push the score toward packed kernels that assume dense KV locality. That explains L2 thrash if real workload is sparse paged reads.

jin: Agreed. My quick probe: when we cap hotspot window to 1000 ops the chooser prefers lazy_epilogue and regression goes away. Running bench: 
```
make bench-packed-attn TARGET=paged_kv BATCH=64 SEQ=1024
# then perf record -g --norecord --output=flame.raw ./bench
```

perf-bot: New perf run registered: fused_attn_batched_kv_hotpath / run_id=2354999987 — baseline vs current. See https://perf.internal/r/2354999987

alex_m: Two possible fixes: 1) Smooth the hotspot metric (exponential decay) so short spikes don't dominate; 2) Add a bump for measured L2 miss rate into selector cost so kernels that increase miss rate get penalized. Option 1 is low-risk.

cora: I prototyped option 1 — changed sampler to EMA with alpha=0.04 and ran local bench: new perf ~0.98x baseline. No regression. I'll open a draft PR.

matteo: Nice. But also think about the epilogue prefetch flag — we shipped it enabled by default. We should gate it with a runtime heuristic: if seq_len > 512 and avg_kv_hit_density < 0.25 then prefer lazy_epilogue. That prevents eager prefetch on sparse paged KV.

jin: +1. Quick patch: 
```
if seq_len > 512 and kv_density < 0.25:
    prefer_kernel('lazy_epilogue')
```

cora: I'll add that heuristic to the selector and add a unit test that simulates sparse paged reads. Also will add a perf regression CI target for B=64 S=1024 so we catch this class earlier.

perf-bot: Quick follow-up run (post-EMA change) shows improvement: 0.99x baseline, L2 miss delta -2%. run_id=2355000123

alex_m: Good. Can we also record a small flamegraph snapshot in the rollforward notes so oncall can triage later? Link the flame in the PR.

cora: Will do. Opening PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/runtime/pull/3142 (draft) — includes EMA sampler alpha=0.04, new selector heuristic, and a bench CI job for the paged-KV hotspot.

matteo: Thx. Once review + perf CI green, let's canary the PR behind a feature flag for Dedicated only for 24h before rolling to Hosted. :thumbsup:

cora: Sounds good. I'll drop a note in #eng-releases when canary is running.

jin: One last note — double-check interaction with quantized kernels. Packed QKV quantized path uses different memory layout and the L2 pressure there is worse. If we flip heuristics we should validate q8/q4 paths too.

cora: Yup will add q8/q4 CI permutations.

perf-bot: Canary run (post-PR, gated) metrics: B=64 S=1024 q8 path: 0.98x baseline. No regression observed — run_id=2355000345

cora: Thanks everyone. Follow-up items: 1) finish PR + tests, 2) add flamegraph to PR, 3) validate quantized paths, 4) monitor perf CI for 48h. I'll post an update in ~2d. :slightly_smiling_face:
